new_scholarship.description: The Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship is a merit award for international students commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Adelaide University, offering a 50% tuition fee reduction over the standard full-time duration of the degree. Places are limited and allocated on merit by a selection panel reviewing applications on a rolling basis through the recruitment cycle. Applicants must be international students applying to a CRICOS-registered bachelor or master degree that is not on the Excluded Programs list, and must have an ATAR of 99 or an overall GPA of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale as the basis of admission. programme_detail_official.description: The University of Sydney International Stipend Scholarship (USYDIS) provides financial support to international postgraduate research students, both commencing and already enrolled, in a higher degree by research. It is competitively awarded and pays a stipend of $44,293 per annum at the 2027 rate together with relocation and thesis allowances. Every USYDIS holder is automatically awarded the companion University of Sydney Tuition Fee Scholarship, which provides 100% of tuition fees for up to 14 research periods along with Overseas Student Health Cover, so the combined award covers fees, living costs and basic relocation for international research students. Preference may be given to applicants entering a PhD and to applicants without a prior HDR degree or equivalent scholarship at the same level.

new_scholarship.description: The Deakin Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship recognises international students with consistently high academic performance and the potential to make a leading contribution to Deakin and the communities it serves. The award covers 100% or 50% of tuition fees depending on the scholarship outcome, for the normal duration of the program, and requires participation in the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program. Applicants must be new international students enrolling in a Deakin coursework degree with at least an 85% average or equivalent in previous studies, and must submit a 300-word personal statement, two references and their academic transcripts. Scholarships are assessed on a rolling basis in the lead-up to each trimester, and the award is not available to the Doctor of Medicine (H911) program.

programme_detail_official.description: The QUT International Merit Scholarship is a high-achievement award for future international undergraduate and postgraduate students. QUT's own international student scholarships hub states that it covers 25% of tuition fees for the full duration of the program provided the recipient meets the minimum academic standards of the course, and that it is available in selected faculties only. Recipients on the QUT site include students of the Bachelor of Information Technology (Computer Science), the Master of Architecture and the Master of Business (International Business), confirming it spans both undergraduate and postgraduate study.

logo_override.validation_detail: jpg, 1200x1200, on www.qut.edu.au - declared by QUT itself as its og:image. Note on method: three webfetch probes of this asset timed out, so the confirmation came from a real browser loading the URL over HTTPS and decoding it as a 1200x1200 opaque image (1,134,152 dark / 298,830 light / 7,018 mid opaque pixels). Because the file is fully opaque with a dominant dark field rather than a transparent white wordmark, it stays visible on a light card as a dark logo tile.

research_notes.logo: QUT's header mark is delivered to assistive technology as the text link "QUT" rather than an image, so no img[src*=logo] exists in the page markup. The only logo asset QUT publishes on its own domain that page declares is its og:image, https://www.qut.edu.au/__data/assets/image/0007/909781/qut-logo-og-1200.jpg (declared alongside og:image:width 1200 and og:image:height 1200). I probed it three times with webfetch and all three attempts timed out, so I confirmed it a different way: loading the URL in a real browser over HTTPS decoded it as a fully opaque 1200x1200 image with a dominant dark field, which both proves the asset resolves on the awarding body's own domain and shows it is a dark-on-light-field tile rather than a white-on-transparent wordmark. The site's favicon, https://www.qut.edu.au/favicon.ico (32x32, 790 dark / 169 light / 65 mid opaque pixels, also browser-confirmed), is the fallback. I am flagging the probe method explicitly because it differs from the standard webfetch confirmation.
